Strong understanding of clinical trial processes from start-up through closeout. In-depth knowledge of Good Clinical Practice (ICH-GCP), regulatory requirements, and clinical research standards. review_candidates.description: Apply now Job no: 596028 Contract type: Fixed Term Appointment Duty Station: Maputo Location: Mozambique Categories: Education UNICEF works in over 190 countries and territories to save children’s lives, defend their rights, and help them fulfill their potential, from early childhood through adolescence. At UNICEF, we are committed, passionate, and proud of what we do for as long as we are needed. Promoting the rights of every child is not just a job – it is a calling. UNICEF is a place where careers are built: we offer our staff diverse opportunities for professional and personal development that will help them reinforce a sense of purpose while serving children and communities across the world. We welcome everyone who wants to belong and grow in a diverse and passionate culture, coupled with an attractive compensation and benefits package. Visit our website to learn more about what we do at UNICEF. For every child, the right to Education How can you make a difference? Mozambique has one of the youngest populations in the world, with 65 per cent of the population under the age of 24. This demographic profile presents a major opportunity for national development, but only if children, adolescents and young people acquire the foundational, transferable, digital and market-relevant skills needed for further learning, decent work and civic participation. Despite progress in expanding access to education, learning outcomes remain weak, completion rates are low, and many learners leave school without basic literacy and numeracy skills or the competencies required to transition successfully to adulthood. The education system is increasingly overstretched by rapid population growth, limited fiscal space, climate shocks, insecurity and persistent inequities. Schools often lack safe, inclusive and resilient learning environments, sufficient trained teachers, adequate materials and effective accountability systems. Adolescents and young people, particularly vulnerable girls, young people with disabilities and those affected by crisis, also face limited access to relevant skills, second-chance learning, safe spaces, services, information, earning opportunities and meaningful participation. The UNICEF Mozambique Country Programme 2027–2030 responds to these challenges through the Learning, Skills and Engagement programme, which aims to strengthen the education system and youth participation mechanisms so that children and adolescents access quality learning opportunities, acquire relevant skills and participate meaningfully in shaping their futures. The programme is structured around three mutually reinforcing outputs: inclusive digital learning solutions; school and system level accountability, safeguarding and preparedness; and pathways for adolescents and young people—especially vulnerable girls—to move from learning to earning while strengthening agency, resilience and civic engagement. Within this architecture, youth engagement, digital transformation and Learning-to-Earning are not stand-alone streams, but mutually reinforcing approaches that support more flexible, inclusive and resilient learning and skills pathways. UNICEF will support government-led efforts to embed these approaches in national systems, using evidence, partnerships and coherent programme standards to improve quality, accountability, continuity during shocks and opportunities for adolescents and young people. Under the overall guidance of the Deputy Representative, Programmes, the Chief Education (Learning, Skills and Engagement) provides strategic leadership and oversight for UNICEF Mozambique’s LSE programme. The Chief is accountable for the quality, coherence and results of integrated strategies that improve foundational learning, expand inclusive learning and skills pathways, strengthen education system resilience and accountability, and enable adolescents and young people to participate meaningfully and transition towards further learning, work and earning opportunities.
